editorial:
Imagine being the scariest guy in school, the kind of person everyone avoids in the halls. That is Joong-pil, a high school bully who spends his days smoking, swearing, and picking on younger kids. He has a reputation to keep up, but everything changes the moment he falls for a girl in his class. Suddenly, being a jerk does not feel so great. You get to watch him struggle as he tries to trade his toughness for kindness, wondering if he can actually be a good person or if he is just born to be a troublemaker. It is a sweet, funny ride that captures that awkward feeling of your first real crush.

The acting is great because you can really feel Joong-pil's confusion as he tries to change his ways. The pacing is snappy and the comedy hits just right, though some of the drama might feel a bit old-school. If you love stories about bad boys turning good, you will enjoy this one. You should definitely try to find this to stream in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for the best picture, or just rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night. If you are a collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a solid move.
endingExplained: By the end, Joong-pil realizes that being feared is not nearly as rewarding as being loved. He stops leaning on his toughness and finally shows his true, softer side to the girl he likes. He manages to leave his bully past behind and makes peace with the people he used to push around. The movie wraps up with him finding a new sense of identity and a hopeful start to a real relationship.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves coming-of-age stories and romantic comedies.
